openers: I have a worry. Can you help?
Can we talk in a quiet place?
trusted_behaviours: They help in a safe way.
scene: A pupil is not sure where to put their class work. The pupil feels worried. They ask a teaching assistant for help.

model.speaker: Story pupil
model.line: I am not sure where my work goes.

model.speaker: Teaching assistant
model.line: We can check the right place together.

busy_model: If the adult is busy, the story pupil can ask when to talk or try another trusted adult. If the worry is still there, keep asking for help.
privacy_pupil: Use the made-up story in class. For a real worry, ask a trusted adult in private. You can pass, point or ask for help.

private_card.title: My trusted adults
private_card.instruction: Choose role types in private. You can write, draw or point. Leave a space blank if you wish. Keep this card.
private_card.help: Not sure who to choose? Ask for help in private. You do not have to fill both spaces.
private_card.note: Use roles, not names. Do not show this card to the group.

safeguarding: If a pupil cannot identify a trusted adult, support them privately and do not press them. Offer a familiar school role and help make contact through the school route; accept a blank card or pass. Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures where needed. Do not write disclosure details in this pack, the private card, a book task or shared learning evidence. Do not read private cards aloud, collect or photograph them for assessment. Staff may support completion only with pupil agreement; the pupil keeps the card.
practice_rule: All classroom prompts and role play use the invented story. Reading a first-person opener is speaking as the fictional pupil, never a request to describe the learner's own worry. A pupil may speak, read, point/select through their usual communication aid, or ask the TA to voice their selected opener. Record the mode and all content prompts. An observer/pass alternative is valid; record practice not observed and plan a later supported opportunity. Never infer an actual disclosure or real-life help-seeking.
independence: Normal word bank, sentence starter, visible model, role card and usual aids stay on all routes. Independent means the learner selects a suitable adult role and initiates the fictional conversation using their usual mode after a general cue, without adult next-step content prompts. Do not remove access aids. TA voicing of a pupil's exact selected words is communication access, not independent spoken speech; record it precisely.

routes.Supported: Model one step, offer two role/opener choices, then hand back the turn. Keep all Level 2 aids and usual communication access. Record actual adult prompts.
routes.Independent: Keep all Level 2 aids. Learner chooses a safe role and opener and starts the fictional talk after the general cue, using their usual mode. Log any next-step content prompts.
routes.Aspire: Keep all Level 2 aids. Try the busy-adult version or explain a next safe option if the worry remains. No extra writing or personal worry is required.

success: Choose a safe adult role for the story.
Use an opener to start the story talk.
Show a next safe step if the adult is busy.
timing: 0–3 calm story starter; 3–7 roles and safe help; 7–11 TA model and check; 11–12 reset.
12–17 teach and rehearse openers; 17–20 private hinge; 20–24 plan one role play; 24–25 reset.
25–33 private TA role-play turns; 33–36 private role-type card; 36–38 next step and response; 38–40 private exit.

scaffolds.start: If the adult is busy, they could ... .
scaffolds.model: They could ask when to talk or try another trusted adult.

scaffolds.start: They will ask ... . They could say ... .
scaffolds.model: They will ask a teaching assistant. They could say: Can I talk to you?

scaffolds.start: In the story, they could say ... .
scaffolds.model: In the story, they could say: I am not sure where my work goes.
Their next step could be to ask another trusted adult.

hinge.question: The adult is busy. What could the story pupil do?
hinge.A: Give up and keep the worry.
hinge.B: Ask when to talk or try another trusted adult.
hinge.decision: Check privately by pointing, speaking or usual aid. If B and a safe reason/choice, proceed. If A, unclear or no response, re-model the busy-adult reply, offer two choices and use the parallel check; do not treat pass as misunderstanding.

parallel.question: The worry is still there after a talk. What could the story pupil do?
parallel.A: Ask a trusted adult again or try another trusted adult.

misconceptions: Any adult must be trusted because of their role.
A role is a possible starting point. A trusted adult listens, takes the worry seriously and helps safely. Support pupils to identify someone appropriate; no pupil has to endorse any adult.
A quiet talk means a secret, or one talk must fix the worry.
Use a school-agreed quiet place with normal supervision. Staff may need to pass on concerns to help keep the pupil safe. If the worry remains, keep asking a trusted adult for help.

adaptations.Cognition & Learning: Three openers, one mild story, one step at a time; read aloud, visible model, two choices and reduced repetitions. Keep explicit instruction, scaffolding and flexible grouping.
adaptations.Communication & Interaction: Wait time, familiar aid, pointing/selection, role cards and exact TA voicing/readback. Do not require eye contact or speech.
adaptations.SEMH: Predictable story-only tasks; no public personal questioning. Pass, observer role, quiet pause and supported return. Do not ask pupils to explain a pass.
adaptations.Sensory/Physical: Usual safe seating, accessible print and communication aid; quiet reset without sudden sound or forced movement.
adaptations.EAL: Plan in any language. Explain worry, trusted, role and opener with short examples. Accept chosen words through usual language support.

cold_call.F: Which role could help the story pupil?
cold_call.M: Which opener could the story pupil choose?
cold_call.H: What could they do if that adult is busy?

ta_focus.I_do: Voice the invented pupil and adult lines calmly. Check one opener by selection; keep all models visible.
ta_focus.We_do: Offer choices and wait. Practise the story with the learner's usual mode; record content prompts separately from access.
ta_focus.Independent: Offer private turns and the observer/pass route. Support private role-type card only with agreement; do not collect it. Route any concern through safeguarding.

evidence: Use Evidence Sheet for anonymous/session learning notes: adult-role choice for the invented scene, selected opener, observed initiation/usual mode, next safe step, access and content prompts, one NS and learner response. No personal adult roles from the private card, names or worries. Observed with prompts, observed without next-step prompts and not observed are distinct. This is formative lesson practice, not proof of real-life disclosure or help-seeking.
marking: VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in green; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E actual evidence banked; R responded. R only when Voice and Audience are present, one NS is set and the pupil responds in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm mapping.
where_this_leads: This helps me ask for support when I learn or do a job.
cold_call_label: Optional private fictional check prompts; never public personal questions.
quiet_place_note: An adult chooses a school-agreed quiet place with normal supervision. Quiet does not mean secret or isolated.

Use the made-up story in class. For a real worry, ask a trusted adult in private.
A pupil is not sure where to put their class work. The pupil feels worried. They ask a teaching assistant for help.
Pick an adult role for the story. Pick an opener. Show what the story pupil could do if the adult is busy. Point, say or use your usual aid. A scribe can write your words and read them back.
Use the story with a teaching assistant. Your card and aids stay. Read an opener, point to one or ask the adult to voice your choice. You can watch, pass or stop.

Keep your first try. Use one next step. Reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Do not write a real worry or adult’s name here.
Ask for help in private. If one adult is busy, ask when to talk or try another trusted adult. You can pass and come back with help.
Use a work code, not a name. Log the story task. Keep real worries, names and roles from the private card out of this sheet. Use the school’s own safe record for real concerns.

States: started with no step cues; started with step cues; try not seen this time. A step cue tells what to say next. Log speech, point, aid or exact TA voicing. If the TA reads out the pupil’s chosen words, log that help. Do not call it the pupil’s own speech.

No adult to choose? Give help in private. Do not press. If a pupil shares a real worry, pass it to the safeguarding lead. Use the school route. Listen and give calm support. Do not probe or promise to keep a secret. Keep real details out of this pack and shared work.
E: real work saved. R: only with Voice, Audience, one NS and a reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio.

paragraphs: Talk about a worry with a trusted adult (Time to Talk). All classroom prompts and role play use the invented story. Reading a first-person opener is speaking as the fictional pupil, never a request to describe the learner's own worry. A pupil may speak, read, point/select through their usual communication aid, or ask the TA to voice their selected opener. Record the mode and all content prompts. An observer/pass alternative is valid; record practice not observed and plan a later supported opportunity. Never infer an actual disclosure or real-life help-seeking.

Possible types are teacher, teaching assistant, parent or carer, and school support adult. A role does not guarantee trust. Teach the signs: listens, takes a worry seriously, helps safely. No pupil must endorse any particular adult or supply a personal name.

BUILD · three to four learners · Spring 1 Week 4 · formative
Theme Resilience & Change. Six-week term; Week 6 assessing.
Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T none).
Talk about a worry with a trusted adult (Time to Talk).
Source: BUILD Weekly Spring row 67, as supplied in the owner brief. The workbook was not reopened; no independent cell check is claimed.

Identify a possible trusted adult by role, recognise listening and safe help, choose one of three conversation openers and practise the invented classroom worry with a teaching assistant. The private role-type card stays with the pupil. Classroom evidence uses the story only.

Books; Support Cards pages 1–6; vocabulary; three-opener keep card on page 2; private My trusted adults card on page 4; private staff record. Agree the supervised quiet talk space and school help route. Confirm accessible print and usual communication aids. Do not plan personal worry questions.
This helps me ask for support when I learn or do a job.
Chunks last 12, 13 and 15 minutes. Two one-minute resets are inside the 40 minutes. Reduce repetition for access. Keep observer/pass and supported return available.

0–3: read the calm invented story and ask which role could help. 3–7: teach that a trusted adult listens, takes a worry seriously and helps safely. A role offers a possible starting point, not proof that every adult is trusted. 7–11: TA models both story roles, then checks an opener privately by selection. 11–12: quiet reset with usual access.

12–17: teach the three exact openers on the keep card. Rehearse one selected opener in the story. 17–20: main hinge B and parallel A, using pointing, speech or usual aid. 20–24: choose an adult role and plan a story conversation with the visible model. 24–25: quiet reset.

25–33: offer private TA role-play turns. Peers use the neutral story reference; do not perform personal worries to the class. 33–36: pupil may fill the role-type card privately, with agreed support, and keeps it. 36–38: one next step and response. 38–40: private story exit and keep both cards.
Model one step, offer two role/opener choices, then hand back the turn. Keep all Level 2 aids and usual communication access. Record actual adult prompts.
Keep all Level 2 aids. Learner chooses a safe role and opener and starts the fictional talk after the general cue, using their usual mode. Log any next-step content prompts.
Keep all Level 2 aids. Try the busy-adult version or explain a next safe option if the worry remains. No extra writing or personal worry is required.

Model the full story dialogue first. Next, keep the dialogue and opener card visible while the pupil selects an opener. For a later observed turn, give a general task cue and fade next-step content prompts only. Do not remove normal reading, language, sensory or communication access. Record further teaching and later use separately.

An exact scribe or TA may voice the pupil’s selected words, read them back and permit correction. Record the mode precisely. TA voicing is communication access; it is not independent spoken speech. An adult-chosen or modelled answer is supported learning. A completed card does not prove a conversation happened.

I do: model calmly and check an opener. We do: offer choices and wait. Independent: offer private turns and pass; support the private card only with agreement. Do not collect it; route concerns through safeguarding.
Level 2 word bank, sentence starter and visible model stay on all routes for every task. All seven sets are also on Support Cards pages 5–6.
Model: The pupil could ask a teaching assistant.

Model: They could say: I have a worry. Can you help?

1 Point to the place or instruction. 2 Ask a short question privately. 3 Rephrase. 4 Offer a scaffold or choice. 5 Model the first step only, then return the task. Allow processing time. Log next-step content prompts during observed initiation; keep them separate from normal access.
Choose a safe adult role for the story.
Use an opener to start the story talk.
Show a next safe step if the adult is busy.
Ask which line starts the talk. Accept selection of an opener from the card, through usual mode. Re-model if needed. Do not ask what the pupil is worried about. A pass is not a wrong answer.

The adult is busy. What could the story pupil do? A: Give up and keep the worry. B: Ask when to talk or try another trusted adult. Correct B. Check privately by pointing, speaking or usual aid. If B and a safe reason/choice, proceed. If A, unclear or no response, re-model the busy-adult reply, offer two choices and use the parallel check; do not treat pass as misunderstanding.

The worry is still there after a talk. What could the story pupil do? A: Ask a trusted adult again or try another trusted adult. B: Stop asking for help. Correct A. Recheck privately and record support; a pass remains unobserved.
Three openers, one mild story, one step at a time; read aloud, visible model, two choices and reduced repetitions. Keep explicit instruction, scaffolding and flexible grouping.
Wait time, familiar aid, pointing/selection, role cards and exact TA voicing/readback. Do not require eye contact or speech.
Predictable story-only tasks; no public personal questioning. Pass, observer role, quiet pause and supported return. Do not ask pupils to explain a pass.
Usual safe seating, accessible print and communication aid; quiet reset without sudden sound or forced movement.
Plan in any language. Explain worry, trusted, role and opener with short examples. Accept chosen words through usual language support.

Use story-only questions with prior invitation; allow pointing or pass. F: Which role could help the story pupil? M: Which opener could the story pupil choose? H: What could they do if that adult is busy?

A role alone does not guarantee trust: look for listening and safe help; do not press an endorsement. A quiet talk is not a secrecy promise: staff may share safety concerns. If the worry remains, ask again or try another trusted adult.

If a pupil cannot identify a trusted adult, support them privately and do not press them. Offer a familiar school role and help make contact through the school route; accept a blank card or pass. Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures where needed. Do not write disclosure details in this pack, the private card, a book task or shared learning evidence. Do not read private cards aloud, collect or photograph them for assessment. Staff may support completion only with pupil agreement; the pupil keeps the card.

Use the invented story only. Normal aids, card and model stay. Record selected words, usual mode and any exact TA voicing separately from adult next-step content prompts. An observer/pass is valid; record practice not observed. Do not infer a real disclosure or real-life help-seeking.

Use Evidence Sheet for anonymous/session learning notes: adult-role choice for the invented scene, selected opener, observed initiation/usual mode, next safe step, access and content prompts, one NS and learner response. No personal adult roles from the private card, names or worries. Observed with prompts, observed without next-step prompts and not observed are distinct. This is formative lesson practice, not proof of real-life disclosure or help-seeking.

Observed initiation without adult next-step content prompts; Observed initiation with adult next-step content prompts; Practice not observed this time. Record the actual role choice for the story, opener, mode, visible initiation and next safe step. Do not infer real-life help-seeking or disclosure from the fictional practice.

VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in green; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E actual evidence banked; R responded. R only when Voice and Audience are present, one NS is set and the pupil responds in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm mapping.

Use books or normal response aids for the invented scene. The two keep cards are the intentional fill-in exception. No private-card content, names or real worry goes into books, photographs or shared evidence. Plan in any language.
Week 4 is formative within the six-week term. Week 6 is assessing. Only Week 4 is authored here. The exact outcome is retained, with generic teaching content and no separate named campaign material.
